title: Prototype-Guided Optimization of Quantum Data Embeddings with Linear Cost
abstract: In supervised quantum machine learning with classical data, classification performance critically depends on the geometry induced by quantum data embedding. Existing data-adaptive approaches rely on pairwise fidelity evaluations between samples, which scale as $O(B^2)$ for $B$ samples and create a computational bottleneck in iterative embedding optimization. To address this issue, we propose a prototype-guided framework for efficient data-adaptive quantum embedding. Using class-prototype separation and sample-to-prototype compactness, we derive a measurable lower certificate for class-ensemble distinguishability and construct a prototype-based objective requiring only $O(B)$ fidelity evaluations. We integrate this objective into an end-to-end pipeline that combines task-specific quantum circuit architecture optimization with continuous refinement of the data-embedding parameters. Across five benchmark datasets with up to 20 qubits, our method retains competitive quantum kernel support vector machine (SVM) performance while reducing fidelity-evaluation cost, with particularly strong gains over budget-matched pairwise optimization on T-MNIST. Geometric analyses examine how the learned embeddings relate to kernel alignment and classification margins, revealing dataset-dependent benefits and limitations. We further derive a prototype-based classifier in the reproducing kernel Hilbert space that provides an explicit witness for the SVM objective and a low-cost proxy for model selection, and extend the framework to multiple prototypes for multimodal class structures.
summary: This paper addresses the computational bottleneck in optimizing quantum data embeddings for machine learning by replacing costly pairwise fidelity calculations with an efficient prototype-guided objective. By focusing on class prototypes, the authors reduce the complexity from $O(B^2)$ to $O(B)$, enabling the training of high-performing Quantum Kernel SVMs on larger datasets.
main_problem: Existing data-adaptive quantum embedding optimization methods suffer from a computational bottleneck due to pairwise fidelity evaluations scaling quadratically with the number of samples ($O(B^2)$).
main_result: A prototype-guided framework reduces the complexity to $O(B)$ fidelity evaluations while maintaining competitive Quantum Kernel Support Vector Machine (QKSVM) performance on benchmark datasets.
method: The authors derive a measurable lower certificate for class-ensemble distinguishability using class prototypes and construct a prototype-based objective function combining sample-to-prototype compactness, within-class coherence, and cross-class separation.
model_or_system: The system involves mapping classical data $x$ to a quantum state $|\psi_\Phi(x)angle$ via an $n$-qubit quantum data embedding circuit $U_\Phi(x)$. The optimization is performed on the parameters of this embedding circuit.
key_observables: Class-ensemble distinguishability ($\Delta\Phi$), Pairwise Fidelity Kernel ($k_\Phi$), Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC), and the geometric margin ($e_{mi}$).
important_parameters: The complexity scales are $O(B^2)$ (pairwise) vs. $O(B)$ (prototype-guided); the number of qubits ($n$) and the number of prototypes ($K$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that class-ensemble distinguishability can be effectively bounded and optimized using only prototype-based metrics, avoiding full pairwise comparisons.
figures_summary: Figures compare the computational cost reduction between pairwise and prototype methods, and analyze the resulting geometric separation ($\Delta\Phi,ab$) and QKSVM margin ($e_{mi}$) across different data difficulty levels.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies the $O(B^2)$ bottleneck, then introduces the theoretical framework using class prototypes to derive an $O(B)$ lower certificate for distinguishability. It details the composite objective function ($L_{PG}$) and validates its use in an end-to-end pipeline combining circuit optimization with performance evaluation.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial algorithmic improvement for applying quantum machine learning, transforming an intractable quadratic optimization problem into a linear one, which is vital for scaling QML to real-world datasets.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: Comparison of pairwise and single-prototype-guided quantum embed- ding optimization. (a) Pairwise optimization promotes high fidelity for same-class sample pairs and low fidelity for cross-class pairs, requiring B(B −1)/2 evalua- tions. (b) The proposed method promotes high sample-to-class-prototype fidelity and low cross-class prototype fidelity, reducing the cost to B + 1 evaluations.

Figure 2: Prototype geometry and downstream behavior. VERT means VERTEBRAL. For each seed, ten unique GA circuits with the lowest and highest training prototype losses form the low- and high-loss groups, respectively. (a) Training Cprior, where the dashed line marks the threshold for a non-vacuous positive certificate. (b) Test pairwise-macro CKTA. (c) Test QKSVM MCC. Markers and error bars denote the mean and 95% seed-bootstrap CI.

Figure 3: Multi-prototype optimization on GLASS. (a) Vilolin plots of OOF mini- mum normalized one-vs-one margin distributions for the single-prototype (K = 1) and multi-prototype (K = (2, 1, 3)) model, where the entries of K denote the class- specific numbers of prototypes. The white circle and the bar indicate the median and interquartile range (IQR) of each distribution, respectively. (b) OOF margin gain ver- sus the reduction in sample-to-assigned-prototype trace-distance radius. Quantile-bin means ± standard errors are shown. ρs means the pooled Spearman correlation.

Figure 4: Geometric analysis for the T-MNIST NQE endpoints in Table 1. (a) Exact train class-pair ensemble distance ∆Φ,ab. Each marker represents one of the ten class pairs and reports its average over ten seeds. (b) Mean Test margin gain, ∆em = emPrototype −emPairwise-B, within deciles defined by the leave-one-seed-out Pairwise-B difficulty. Decile 1 contains the hardest 10% of Test samples. Error bars indicate 95% seed-bootstrap intervals.

Figure 4(a) shows that all ten class-pair markers lie above the diagonal. Thus, Prototype increases ∆Φ,ab for every class pair, rather than improving only the macro average. The average of exact class-ensemble distance increases from 0.443 to 0.764, accompanied by an increase in Test MCC from 0.642 to 0.779.
